type: Intraday Power Stack research overlay — Iran/Hormuz escalation + peak-load/cooling stress + AI credit supply
evidencePolicy: This overlay changes theme significance, research priority and action thresholds. It does not mechanically change company fundamental scores. ZeroHedge/sell-side material is treated as a hypothesis input and independently checked where possible against CAISO, company filings and Reuters.
headlineRead: Three fresh signals reinforce one regime rather than three separate trades: Middle East attacks are tightening energy/shipping risk and inflation pressure; California and Malaysia heat are exposing the value of dispatchable power, grid capacity and cooling; and record AI-related borrowing is making financing quality a gating variable. Prefer contracted/operating scarcity and visible backlog over unfunded duration. Do not chase stocks that have already broken above prior entry zones.

currentThemeOrder.name: Middle East Oil / Refined Products / Shipping Risk
currentThemeOrder.whyNow: Iran attacked a US-used base near Al Azraq and ships around Hormuz after US strikes on Iranian tankers; Houthi attacks also hit Saudi energy infrastructure. Hormuz commodity traffic fell to six vessels versus a recent average near twelve and Brent approached $100.

currentThemeOrder.name: Long-End Funding Stress + AI Credit Supply
currentThemeOrder.whyNow: Oil-driven inflation pressure is colliding with a very large AI financing wave. Independent Reuters reporting confirms AI-linked debt supply and investor fatigue, while the attached Goldman/ZeroHedge note points to a temporary late-2026 issuance breather followed by a potentially heavier 2027 supply wave.

currentThemeOrder.name: Power / Grid / Cooling + Peak-Load Resilience
currentThemeOrder.whyNow: CAISO issued a Sep 9 statewide Flex Alert and EEA1 as prolonged heat raises air-conditioning demand while solar output falls in the evening. Malaysia separately reported data-centre power use at a record 9.3% of demand during August heat, versus a 7% 2026 average, with cooling cited as the driver.

currentThemeOrder.name: AI Buildout: Financing + Cash Conversion
currentThemeOrder.whyNow: The physical AI buildout remains real, but lenders and bond investors are requiring stronger permits, leases, guarantees and economics. Funded backlog, signed offtake and short cash-conversion cycles deserve a higher premium.

currentThemeOrder.name: Copper / Grid Input Inflation
currentThemeOrder.whyNow: Record copper prices strengthen scarcity economics while raising equipment and project input costs. Pricing power and pass-through now matter more for ETN/PWR/VMI-style beneficiaries.

currentThemeOrder.name: Energy Security Rerouting + Demand Destruction
currentThemeOrder.whyNow: Alternative export routes, non-OPEC supply and weaker Asian demand still argue against extrapolating an unlimited one-way crude spike even as products, shipping and insurance remain tight.

holdingsImpact.action: HOLD; do not chase geopolitical gaps
holdingsImpact.read: Near-$100 Brent, product tightness and energy-security rerouting support cash flow. Papua LNG remains a separate positive. Keep reversal/demand-destruction risk in the price discipline.

holdingsImpact.action: HOLD; Yinson funding remains the add gate
holdingsImpact.read: Lower Hormuz traffic and attacks on vessels increase tanker tonne-mile, scarcity and war-risk relevance, but also raise insurance/operational risk. The company-specific funding issue still dominates fresh capital.

holdingsImpact.action: HOLD; selective add only on disciplined setup
holdingsImpact.read: Higher oil improves realised-price and customer-budget backdrop, but do not capitalise conflict pricing as permanent.

holdingsImpact.action: HOLD; require funded utilisation and FCF proof
holdingsImpact.read: Malaysia's record 9.3% data-centre share of electricity use during heat directly validates the power-and-cooling bottleneck. The same evidence also raises the value of reliable gas/grid capacity. High yields, copper/input costs and project funding remain the equity-value gates.

holdingsImpact.impact: PARENT THESIS STRONGER / WARRANT RISK UNCHANGED
holdingsImpact.action: Track parent and instrument terms only
holdingsImpact.read: Same YTLPOWR benefit, amplified by expiry, liquidity and time-decay risk.
Oil/inflation and AI-capital competition keep long-end hurdle rates restrictive for catalyst-duration equities.
Peak-load stress is incrementally positive for storage/VPP economics, but higher yields and the unresolved Cybercab regulatory audit dominate near-term risk.

holdingsImpact.impact: POSITIVE ENERGY BETA / NO SCORE CHANGE
holdingsImpact.read: Higher oil supports customer budgets but still does not repair utilisation/work-order execution evidence.

watchlistChanges.reason: Vistra has direct CAISO exposure through Moss Landing gas generation and other West assets; CAISO peak stress makes dispatchable generation/capacity economically relevant now. Existing signed PPAs/Helix funding quality remain superior to speculative load. Sep 8 close around $151.72 is above the old preferred entry, so do not chase.

Grid/electrical scarcity is validated, but Sep 8 close around $422.13 is above the old support-entry zone and around/above prior confirmation. Wait for retest rather than upgrading into price strength.
Transmission/time-to-power remains one of the cleanest beneficiaries of real load, but Sep 8 close around $639.05 is near the prior stronger confirmation area. No chase.

Malaysia data-centre load is now an observed grid fact, not only forecast demand. TNB already supplies operating/under-construction data-centre projects and regulated network capex provides a lower-duration way to own the buildout.

FY26 revenue and profit growth plus an approximately RM1.64bn order book give company-specific proof behind the Malaysia substation/grid thesis. Price near RM3.72 is close to the recent high, so research priority rises faster than buy-now attractiveness.
Direct attacks on Gulf energy/shipping reinforce the value of non-Hormuz LNG corridors and contracted export capacity. Pullback-first remains appropriate.
Iran supports traditional energy-service optionality while the Kelvion acquisition creates a second leg in data-centre cooling. Integration and valuation still matter.
Power and thermal infrastructure remain core beneficiaries, but the AI credit story raises the value of customer funding and signed backlog.
The nuclear theme remains strong, but financing-heavy pre-revenue reactor equities sit on the wrong side of long-end and AI-capital competition.

dashboardTriggers.bullishForCashFlowScarcityTrigger: 10Y holds near/above 4.8% while AI credit spreads/orderbooks deteriorate
